title: Unifying the structures of language in a neural population code
title_zh: 在神经群体编码中统一语言结构
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have mastered human language in ways that no previous computational system has. While rule-based, symbolic systems sufficed for constrained, well-defined problems, they were not able to accommodate the context-sensitive expressivity of natural language. LLMs instead use statistical learning to encode the diversity of linguistic structures into a unified high-dimensional embedding space. Strikingly, this context-driven, distributed representation closely parallels neural population codes, suggesting that the human language system may have converged on a similar computational strategy. Drawing on a growing body of work at the intersection of artificial intelligence and cognitive neuroscience, we show that LLMs can serve as cognitively plausible models of the neural computations supporting language in the human brain. We conclude that explaining how language can emerge from neural population codes, in both biological and artificial systems, will not be achieved through the incremental refinement of algebraic-symbolic theories but will demand new theoretical paradigms.
abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）以前所未有的方式掌握了人类语言。虽然基于规则的符号系统在受限且定义明确的问题上足够用，但无法处理自然语言的上下文敏感表达能力。LLM 改用统计学习，将语言结构的多样性编码到统一的高维嵌入空间中。值得注意的是，这种由上下文驱动的分布式表征与神经群体编码高度相似，提示人类语言系统可能已收敛到类似的计算策略。基于日益增长的人工智能与认知神经科学交叉研究，我们展示了 LLM 可以作为支持人类大脑语言功能的神经计算的认知上可行模型。我们得出的结论是：要解释语言如何在生物系统与人工系统中从神经群体编码中涌现，不能依赖代数-符号理论的逐步细化，而需要新的理论范式。
